provenance.selectionNotes: Eight native English questions and their corresponding answers were selected verbatim, with link markup removed.

documents.title: What is Wikipedia?
documents.body: Wikipedia is an online free-content encyclopedia that you can edit and contribute to. Wikipedia exists to bring knowledge to everyone who seeks it.

documents.title: Who owns Wikipedia?
documents.body: Wikipedia's technical framework is supported by the Wikimedia Foundation, which owns the domain names. The site is run by the community of Wikipedians.

documents.title: Who is responsible for the articles on Wikipedia?
documents.body: Editing is a collaborative effort. Millions of people have contributed information, and anyone can help correct an error or discuss it on the talk page.

documents.title: How can I contact the project?
documents.body: See Wikipedia:Contact us for important links and email addresses. Improvements to a specific article can be suggested on its talk page.

documents.title: Should I create an account?
documents.body: Editors with user names enjoy several benefits, but editing as an unregistered user is acceptable. A user name also keeps an editor's IP address from public view.

documents.title: How do you know if information is correct?
documents.body: Incorrect information is usually corrected quickly because many people read articles and monitor contributions. Readers are encouraged to validate content and provide useful references.

documents.title: How do you prevent people from ruining articles?
documents.body: All changes are registered in a page history, so defacement can be replaced by reverting to an older version. Editors, bots, watchlists, protection, and blocks also help prevent vandalism.

documents.title: Which wiki software does Wikipedia run on?
documents.body: Wikipedia and the other Wikimedia projects use the MediaWiki software to facilitate collaborative editing and storage of page histories.
